# Outbox metrics follow-up with isolated observers

Baseline A is fresh main `551d4d0825dca64b7143d6f18fc2b13baaf1fe0a`; B is #3085 head `453edc0774e81d59c2a5c084997249583097b87b`, which contains A. Use the complete `outbox-adjacent` matrix with unchanged settings: four modes, A1/B/A2 adjacent in one ubuntu-latest job, 480-second warmup and 180-second measurement, 500 rows/batch, 1 KiB messages, three partitions, acks all, idempotence, 128 KiB batches, 5 ms linger, one connection, 64 MiB buffer, metrics sampled once per second. Both revisions build and validate before timing.

Immediately preceding exact-configuration run [34316843349](https://github.com/thomhurst/Dekaf/actions/runs/34316843349) used the same A, predecessor B `a7a73d076f8fd4590edf4d7d278e3a55d7cd3532` and harness `8188be86e21a0e3cba8fb70406121f735e1e9a08`. Its [full reviewed results](https://github.com/thomhurst/Dekaf/pull/3085#issuecomment-5598732014) remain INCONCLUSIVE with losses: legacy metrics-on p99 6.542920/7.855884/6.482873 ms (+20.07%/+21.18%, control -0.92%); renewal metrics-on maximum 22.146125/23.785796/21.104766 ms (+7.40%/+12.70%, control -4.70%). CPU, throughput, p50 and allocation point screens passed, but those gains do not waive latency. Every phase had four workers, 1–6 measured JIT methods, Gen0 activity and zero final leftover work. No JIT event occurred within one second of the retained maxima. Earlier 180-second-warmup results retain their own pins and are not pooled. There is no accepted candidate; fresh main remains the acceptance baseline.

Current B also fixes timer-range validation and evidence portability. This comparison incorporates #3159 infrastructure CPU isolation and host CPU/steal/pressure time series. Previously Python diagnostics could compete with the client, whose approximate CPU occupancy was already close to one physical core. The new experiment tests whether isolated observers improve reproducibility and reveal scheduler/host pressure around latency losses. It does not assume observers caused those losses. In-process recorders remain in client CPU/allocation scope. No workload or acceptance tolerance changes; all phases get identical observer settings. Cross-run differences cannot isolate the timer fix from the harness change.

Retain all samples/maxima and complete histogram/accounting validation. Review 3% throughput/CPU, 5% latency and 1 B/message allocation criteria against both controls, all control drift, measured warmup operations and runtime/stability series. This is a changed experiment and a new product head, not an identical repeat. Missing error/lease-loss/shutdown evidence remains explicit; a completed job cannot set a performance gate to PASS automatically.
